title: Axios
description: Promise-based HTTP client for browser and Node.js.

data.text: Axios is a popular HTTP client that supports promises, interceptors, and automatic JSON transformation.

data.title: Axios GET request

data.text: Rather than repeating the base URL, headers, and error handling at every call site, you create one configured instance. Interceptors run on every request or response and are where authentication headers, retries, and global error handling belong.

data.title: A configured axios instance with interceptors

data.text: Axios rejects the promise for non-2xx responses, so a `try/catch` sees both network failures and HTTP errors. The error carries `response`, `request`, and `config`, which lets you distinguish a 404 from a timeout. `AbortController` cancels an in-flight request, which matters when a component unmounts or a search field changes.

data.title: Typed errors and cancellation
Interview angle: fetch vs axios
data.text: Modern `fetch` covers the basics, so the honest reason to choose axios is interceptors, automatic JSON parsing, request cancellation ergonomics, and a consistent error shape across old browsers. Note that axios does not time out by default — you must set `timeout` — and that its default `xsrf` handling is a reason teams reach for it. Being specific rather than saying "axios is better" is what interviewers look for.
